opennyai_summary.final__facts:
The present application has been filed under  Section 528 BNSS for quashing of the order dated 17.04.2023 in  connection with Gogri P.S. Case No. 553 of 2021 and G.R.
 No.3814 of 2021 by which cognizance under Sections 498A,
504, 506 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code has been taken against Anand Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46992677/
1  the petitioners.
 Patna High Court CR.
3. The allegation is of subjecting the informant -  opposite party no.2 to various sorts of torture due to non-  fulfillment of the demand of the dowry.
5. Both the parties jointly submitted that the matter be  referred for mediation.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
petitioner no. 1 is the husband of the O.P. No.2, petitioner no.2  is the brother of the husband of the O.P. No.2 and the petitioner  no.3 is the mother-in-law of the O.P. No.2
. Learned counsel  further submitted that marriage is a sacred ceremony but little  matrimonial skirmish suddenly erupts into hatred and the parties  ponder to reconcile their dispute outside the court.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is commonly seen in the society that the entire  family members, as well as, relatives are made accused along  with the husband to face criminal prosecution.
8. The law in respect of matrimonial dispute between  husband and wife is well settled, at the same time, the Apex  Court has held that the family members of husband should not  be roped unnecessarily and face vexatious criminal trial.
9. From perusal of the complaint, it is evident that  there is no specific allegation against the petitioner no. 2, who is  the brother of the husband of the opposite party no. 2.
In light of  the recent judgment of Apex Court in the case of Navneesh  Aggarwal & Ors. v. State of Haryana & Anr. reported in 2025  INSC 963, I find that no case under Section 498A/34 of IPC is  made out against the petitioner no. 2.
So far as the petitioner no.1 and 3 are  concerned, this Court finds that the matrimonial dispute is not  an offense against the society rather a matrimonial dispute is a  private conflict between spouses and does not inherently  constitute an offence against society, as has been held by the  Apex Court in the case of B.S. Joshi v. State of Haryana,
 Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.21196 of 2025 dt.03-11-2025  4/7  reported in, (2003) 4 SCC 675, in paragraph nos. 12 and 13 Anand Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46992677/
But little matrimonia  skirmishes suddenly erupt which often assume  serious proportions resulting in commission of  heinous crimes in which elders of the family ar  also involved with the result that those who  could have counselled and brought about  rapprochement are rendered helpless on their  being arrayed as accused in the criminal case.
There are many other reasons which need not be  mentioned here for not encouraging matrimonial  litigation so that the parties may ponder over  their defaults and terminate their disputes  amicably by mutual agreement instead of  fighting it out in a court of law where it take  years and years to conclude and in that process  the parties lose their "young" days in chasing  their "cases" in different courts.
 11.
This Court, in Dara Lakshmi Narayana vs.
 Patna High Court CR.
5/7 Anand Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46992677/
4  State of Telangana, (2025) 3 SCC 735, has made it  clear that family members of the husband ought not  to be unnecessarily roped into criminal proceedings  arising out of matrimonial discord.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
This Court finds it proper in the interest of the petitioner nos. 1  and 3 and wife (opposite party no. 2), as there is no objection to  arrive at a mutual terms and conditions of settlement, for that  certain time is required.
 13.
The parties seek to settle their strained  matrimonial relationship amicably.
The learned District Court  shall also strive till last to settle the dispute outside the Court.
14. Petitioner nos. 1 and 3 and opposite party no. 2  have agreed to appear before the learned District Court on  27.11.2025 at 10:30 AM.
16. Learned Mediator of the District Mediation Center concerned shall make his/her best efforts to settle the dispute between the parties amicably and thereafter submit his/her report before the concerned learned District Court, well within a period of four months, till then, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioner nos.1 and 3 in connection with the aforesaid case.
17. In case, the parties resolve their dispute amicably, Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.21196 of 2025 dt.03-11-2025 then the proceeding is required to be dropped in light of the law laid down by the Apex Court as referred hereinabove.
18.
In case of failure on the part of the petitioner nos.1 and 3 to appear on 27.11.2025 before the learned District Court or any date fixed by the learned Mediator, the interim protection granted to the petitioner nos.1 and 3 shall automatically lose its force.
19. In case, it is deliberate on the part of the petitioner nos.1 and 3 and they fail to reconcile, then in that case, the learned District Court shall proceed with the trial.
In case, it is deliberate on the part Anand Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46992677/
6 of the opposite party no.2 to reconcile, then in that case, continuing with the criminal proceeding will amount to abuse of process of court and the interim protection granted to petitioner nos.1 and 3 shall continue and the proceeding against him is required to be dropped in accordance with law.
20. Accordingly, the present quashing application stands disposed of.
